candidates.attacker_control: A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can get a victim's browser to issue a request (e.g. or /simpleQueueReset/reset) controls all endpoint parameters (itemId as numeric queue id or job display name via findIemByName, MoveAction.java:65-71, 95-104; moveType; viewName) and the timing. Only the victim's session cookies/permissions are used; the plugin adds no per-request token, no @RequirePOST, and no same-origin/origin check.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the endpoints are permission-gated: MoveAction.doMove checks Jenkins.MANAGE (MoveAction.java:63) and ResetAction.doReset checks Jenkins.MANAGE before acting (ResetAction.java:19), and both RootActions hide their URL/icon unless the same permission is held (MoveAction.java:44-52, ResetAction.java:30-58) - so this is not an authorization bypass and the attacker must first have a privileged victim; the impact is therefore bounded (no escalation to ADMINISTER, no anonymous exploitation under a properly configured authorization strategy). Checked whether some other layer enforces POST: no @RequirePOST/@POST/checkCrumb/csrf occurrence exists in any readable source file, and the plugin's own docs advertise plain GET URLs, so no compensating control is present in the snapshot. Also confirmed that read-only endpoints (SimpleQueueUpdateAction's getItems/isFilterQueue/getViewName) are not state-changing, so they are not part of this root cause.
candidates.impact: Cross-site request forgery against the queue-control endpoints. An attacker-controlled page can make a MANAGE/ADMINISTER victim's Jenkins reorder the global build queue (moving arbitrary queued items to the top/bottom, delaying or advancing builds) and can reset all manually set ordering; because the operation installs the plugin's global QueueSorter as a side effect, the attack also permanently changes queue-sorting behavior for the Jenkins instance until the sorter is replaced or Jenkins restarts. Integrity impact on build scheduling/ordering; no direct confidentiality or privilege-escalation effect is demonstrated from this source.
candidates.prerequisites: The plugin must be installed and reachable from the victim's browser. The victim must be authenticated with Overall/Manage (Jenkins.MANAGE) - in the default Jenkins configuration ('logged-in users can do anything') every authenticated user holds ADMINISTER which implies MANAGE - and must have at least one buildable item in the queue for a visible reorder. No interactive confirmation is required because the documented UI itself performs these operations with plain GET links.
candidates.root_cause: MoveAction.doMove (src/main/java/cz/mendelu/xotradov/MoveAction.java:59-93) and ResetAction.doReset (src/main/java/cz/mendelu/xotradov/ResetAction.java:18-29) are public Stapler web methods with side effects, but neither is annotated @RequirePOST (no @RequirePOST / @POST occurrence anywhere in the repository) and no CSRF crumb/token is validated in the plugin. All parameters (itemId, moveType, viewName) are read straight from the request (MoveAction.java:65-73), so a GET query string fully drives the operation. Jenkins' crumb filter only protects non-GET verbs, and the repository's own documentation confirms the intended invocation is a bare GET: docs_src/docs/CLI.md:2-13, 35-63 ('curl "http://jenkins_url/simpleMove/move?moveType=DOWN_FAST&itemId=my-job-name"' and the hover-URL example 'http://jenkins_url/simpleMove/move?moveType=DOWN_FAST&itemId=1074193&viewName=.executors'). The move handler then mutates global, process-wide state without any request-origin check: it installs/replaces the Jenkins queue sorter via setSorter (MoveAction.java:446-454, called from moveToTop/moveUp/moveDown/moveToBottom/putAOnTopOfB/putABelowB) and records ordering desires through SimpleQueueComparator.addDesire (MoveAction.java:174-177, 231-234, 313, 333, 349, 370), then calls Queue.maintain() (MoveAction.java:76). ResetAction.doReset likewise mutates the shared comparator state via SimpleQueueSorter.reset() (ResetAction.java:20-23, SimpleQueueSorter.java:36-40).
candidates.title: Queue-mutating endpoints /simpleMove/move and /simpleQueueReset/reset are triggerable by cross-site GET (no POST requirement, no CSRF token)
candidates.trace: Request GET /simpleMove/move?... -> Stapler dispatches MoveAction.doMove (no @RequirePOST) -> MoveAction.java:61-63 obtains Jenkins/Queue and checks Jenkins.MANAGE with the *victim's* authentication -> lines 65-73 parse attacker-controlled itemId/moveType/viewName -> move() lines 106-112 -> moveToTop/moveUp/moveDown/moveToBottom or the *Filtered variants (lines 114-219) -> setSorter() lines 446-454 installs SimpleQueueSorter wrapping the previous sorter (global, persistent side effect) -> SimpleQueueComparator.addDesire (SimpleQueueComparator.java:53-78) records ordering desires keyed by queue item ids -> resort() line 456-458 / Queue.maintain() line 76 re-sorts buildable items, changing execution order. Parallel path: GET /simpleQueueReset/reset -> doReset (ResetAction.java:18-23) -> SimpleQueueSorter.reset() (SimpleQueueSorter.java:36-40) -> SimpleQueueComparator.resetDesires() + Queue.maintain(). Every step after permission check is driven solely by the request, with no token or POST requirement.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed (no code execution, no Jenkins instance, no HTTP requests sent). Jenkins core's exact behaviour for GET dispatch to do* methods and for crumb enforcement is assumed from framework design and from the repository's documented curl/GET usage (docs_src/docs/CLI.md), not verified against Jenkins 2.414.1 binaries here. The exact severity/impact (e.g. whether any MANAGE victim's queue reorder can be observed or chained) and whether Jenkins would classify this endpoint as protected by any core-level GET safeguard were not verified. Whether the pre-existing UI implementation used GET links or POST forms cannot be checked because src/main/resources (Jelly/JS) is absent from the snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-352 Cross-Site Request Forgery (missing POST/CSRF enforcement on state-changing endpoint); related CWE-650

coverage_summary: Read all 11 Java source files under src/main/java/cz/mendelu/xotradov in full (MoveAction, ResetAction, SimpleQueueUpdateAction, SimpleQueueWidget, SimpleQueueSorter, SimpleQueueComparator, SimpleQueueListener, SimpleQueueSorter, DefaultSorter, MoveType, PermissionHandler, TVAF), plus pom.xml, README.md, docs_src/docs/*, and the generated docs/ HTML + search index (targeted keyword searches: RequirePOST, @POST, csrf, hasPermission, getParameter, getQueueItems, getView, CVE, vulnerab, PermissionHandler, itemId). P1 index used for navigation (get_relation_scope: 63 files, 11 Java parsed, 0 omitted, 140 syntax edges, 199 unresolved calls; no SAST/data-flow/control-flow and no Spring runtime verification) and traced call/containment edges around MoveAction and SimpleQueueUpdateAction; all index hints were re-verified against source text. Files present in the snapshot but not code-reviewed in depth: minified third-party docs assets under docs/assets/javascripts (lunr packs, wordcut, mkdocs-material bundle, minified CSS) - only keyword-grepped, not audited for library CVEs.
limitations: src/main/resources (Jelly templates, JS, images) and src/test are absent from the assigned snapshot, so the UI-side rendering/escaping logic and any existing permission/CSRF tests could not be inspected; the missing Jelly cannot confirm whether the pre-fix UI used GET links or POST forms.

No compilation, tests, or Jenkins instance were run; Jenkins core 2.414.1 behaviour (Jenkins.MANAGE semantics, View.getQueueItems permission filtering, Stapler GET dispatch, crumb filter scope) is reasoned from framework knowledge and repository docs, not verified against core source.
The vendored minified third-party JavaScript in docs/ was not audited for known library vulnerabilities; it is generated documentation output, not plugin runtime code.

The P1 relation index is syntactic only (no data-flow, control-flow, semantic resolution, or reachability), so index edges were used only as navigation hints and every cited path was confirmed by reading the file.

rejected_leads.lead: SimpleQueueUpdateAction.getItems()/isFilterQueue()/getViewName() trust the client-supplied 'name' parameter and return the view's queue items with only Overall/Read (SimpleQueueUpdateAction.java:31-63), which could disclose queue metadata for jobs/views the user cannot read.
rejected_leads.reason: The read-only getters do perform a permission check (Jenkins.get().hasPermission(Permission.READ)) and the endpoint's purpose is rendering the queue widget for read users; whether this leaks anything beyond what Jenkins core already shows on /queue depends on unverified core semantics (Jenkins.getView + View.getQueueItems item-level filtering) that are not present in this snapshot, so the evidence threshold is not met.

rejected_leads.lead: SimpleQueueComparator is non-transitive (desires can form cycles A>B, B>C, C>A, SimpleQueueComparator.java:31-46, 53-78) and is an unsynchronized static singleton (Hashtable of mutable ArrayLists) read by Collections.sort in SimpleQueueSorter.sortBuildableItems (SimpleQueueSorter.java:26-31); Collections.sort(TimSort) can throw IllegalArgumentException and break queue maintenance (availability impact).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a user who already holds Overall/Manage (or a CSRF victim holding it) to create the desire set, and the exception is JVM/TimSort-dependent and not provable from the snapshot; lower security impact than the selected candidate, so recorded as unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: TVAF extends TransientViewActionFactory without @Extension (TVAF.java:9-15), and MoveAction.getTop() uses a pointless iterator loop (MoveAction.java:285-296), and MoveAction.doMove uses a single '&' instead of '&&' (MoveAction.java:63).
rejected_leads.reason: Dead/broken wiring and style-level defects with no demonstrated security impact; getTop() functionally still returns the first element because a new iterator is created each iteration, so no exploitable behaviour could be shown.

summary: Scope: the assigned snapshot is the Jenkins "Simple Queue" plugin at 1.4.7-SNAPSHOT (pom.xml targets Jenkins 2.414.1). The only program source is 11 Java files under src/main/java/cz/mendelu/xotradov; all 11 were read in full, and I additionally inspected pom.xml, README.md, docs_src/ and the generated docs/ (keyword searches for RequirePOST, @POST, csrf, hasPermission, getParameter, getQueueItems, CVE, "vulnerab" etc.). The strongest source-supported issue is that both state-changing HTTP endpoints of the plugin (MoveAction.doMove -> /simpleMove/move, ResetAction.doReset -> /simpleQueueReset/reset) are reachable with a plain GET and carry no POST/CSRF enforcement anywhere in the repository, even though the documented UI/CLI invocation is a GET URL. This is a classic CSRF/missing-POST-requirement weakness (CWE-352) for a Jenkins plugin: reordering/installing the global queue sorter (and resetting desires) can be triggered by a cross-site request from a page the victim visits, using only the victim's MANAGE/ADMINISTER session. I selected this as the single candidate; other leads (permission level of the /updateQueue AJAX getters, comparator inconsistency/thread-safety causing sort exceptions, dead TVAF extension) are recorded as rejected/unconfirmed.
